title: WPSS/233/2013 of NARAYAN SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 233 of 2013
Narayan Singh Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & another Ö Respondents
Mr. B.M. Pingal, Advocate, present for the petitioner
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner before this Court seeks
appointment on compassionate ground as his father,
who was Peon in the Revenue services in this State,
died while in harness on 27.07.2011. On August 2011,
the petitioner moved an application for appointment on
compassionate ground under the provision of U.P.
Recruitment of Dependents of Government Servants
Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 (hereinafter referred to as
ëDying in Harness Rules), which has been rejected vide
an order dated 17.10.2011 and consequential order
dated 13.04.2012 passed by the District Magistrate and
State Government respectively on the ground that the
petitioner cannot be given appointment in view of
Section 5(1) of the Dying in Harness Rules, 1974, as his
younger brother is a constable in Police Armed
Constabulary (P.A.C.).
 2. In the counter affidavit, the stand of the State
Government is that the younger brother of the petitioner
is employed and he stays in the same family hence the
petitioner is not qualified for the post in dying in harness
in view of Section 5(1) of Dying in Harness Rules. Section
5(1) of the said Rules is quoted hereunder:-

2
ì5. Recruitment of a member of the family of
the deceased. ñ (1) In case a Government servant
dies in harness after the commencement of these
rules and the spouse of the deceased Government
servant is not already employed under the Central
Government or a State Government or a
Corporation owned or controlled by the Central
Government or a State Government, one member
of his family who is not already employed under
the Central Government or a State Government or
a Corporation owned or controlled by the Central
Government or a State Government shall, on
making an application for the purposes, be given a
suitable employment in Government service on a
post except the post which is within the purview of
the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission, in
relaxation of the normal recruitment rules if such
person ñ
(i) fulfils the educational qualifications
prescribed for the post,
(ii) is otherwise qualified for Government
service, and
(iii) makes the application for employment
within five years from the date of the death of the
Government servant :
Provided that where the State Government is
satisfied that the time-limit fixed for making the
application for employment causes undue
hardship in any particular case, it may dispense
with or relax the requirement as it may consider

3
necessary for dealing with the case in a just and
equitable manner.
(2) As far as possible, such an employment
should be given in the same department in which
the deceased Government servant was employed
prior to his death.]
[3) Each appointment under sub-rule (1) should be
under the condition that the person appointed
under sub-rule (1) shall upkeep those other family
members of the deceased Government servant who
are incapable for their own maintenance and were
dependant of the abovesaid deceased Government
servant immediately before his death.]î
 3. Under the aforesaid provision, the only
embargo on compassionate appointment is that the
spouse of the deceased should not be employed with a
Central Government or a State Government or a
Corporation.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied
upon the decision of this Court in State of Uttarakhand
& others Vs Ajay Kumar & another decided on
30.04.2010 (SPA No. 25 of 2010) wherein it has been
held that merely because the brother of the petitioner has
been employed, it would not disqualify the petitioner for
applying under the Dying-in-Harness Rules.
5. The petitioner, who seeks appointment, is
admittedly comes within the definition of family under the
said Rules. The fact that the brother of the petitioner,

4
who is the son of the deceased, is gainfully employed does
not bar the petitioner from the eligibility on appointment
on compassionate ground. As the father of the petitioner
was Peon, the petitioner is liable to be considered on a
Class IV post in the Revenue Service.
6. In view of the above fact as well as considering
the above judgment of this Court, the impugned orders
dated 17.10.2011 and 13.04.2012 are quashed. I direct
the respondents to give appointment to the petitioner on
the post of Class IV since the only ground for rejecting the
claim of the petitioner is that the brother of the deceased
was employed and the same is passed on a wrong
interpretation, in fact, misreading of Section 5 of the
Dying in Harness Rules.
7. The writ petition is allowed in terms of the
above terms.
8. No order as to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
09.09.2013
Aswal
